focus.jbig: Jobs report at 8:30 · war still live · scanner boarded nothing
focus.jtag: August NFP is the marquee event; VIX cratered to ~14 on Waller, but oil holds ~$92 and hike odds are a coin-flip
focus.jnote: The tape is calmer than earlier this week, but the event risk is front-and-center. The August jobs report lands at 8:30 ET — consensus is a soft ~55–58K rebound from July’s −23K, with unemployment ~4.1%. Crucially the reaction function is inverted: after Chair Warsh’s hawkish Jackson Hole tone, a HOT print raises September hike odds while a SOFT print takes hike risk off the table. Fed Governor Waller then eased the pressure Thursday, saying he’d support holding rates if inflation keeps cooling — that dropped hike odds from ~70% toward a coin-flip, sent the VIX tumbling to ~14.3, pushed the dollar to a May low, and drove a broad rally (S&P +1.1%, Dow +624). Meanwhile the U.S.–Iran fight is still live — crude holds ~$92 WTI / ~$95 Brent on constrained Hormuz flows. Live macro event plus a two-sided war is not a premium-selling setup.
focus.notdown: Energy (XLE, XOM, MPC) and Defense (LMT, RTX, NOC) remain the groups with a fundamental bid — oil supply fear lifts energy, conflict-demand lifts defense. But these are two-sided war trades, not clean Snipers: one Hormuz-reopening or de-escalation headline gaps them straight back down. The scanner found no qualifying energy or defense name that cleared the gate today. Watch-only.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive growth got a big relief bid Thursday on Waller’s dovish shift, but selling bear calls into that squeeze — with a jobs print in the next few hours that could reprice the whole curve either way — is exactly the blow-up 4-VAL exists to prevent. The disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today and wait for the print to clear.
focus.why: Why RED? By rule, NFP inside the next 24h locks out GREEN — you cannot sell premium into a marquee macro print. Composite 58 is squarely WARM and P(≥1% gap) at 40% is above the 35% trigger, either of which alone also blocks GREEN. Layer on a live U.S.–Iran military exchange with oil near $92 and a three-day weekend (Labor Day Monday) that stretches the headline-risk window, and the overnight tail is unquantifiable. The scanner boarded ZERO names — nothing cleared the gate across all three setup types. Stand down on new credit spreads. Cash is a position today.

risks: August NFP · 8:30 ET today — consensus ~55–58K after July’s −23K; the reaction is inverted, so a HOT print raises September hike odds and a SOFT one lowers them. The single biggest event of the day — index-wide, two-sided gap risk.

Iran retaliation & Strait of Hormuz — fresh U.S. strikes this week drew Iranian attacks on Gulf bases; roughly a fifth of the world’s oil moves through Hormuz and flows are still constrained. Any escalation or closure sends crude vertical — the week’s biggest tail.

Long-weekend headline gap — markets are closed Monday for Labor Day; three overnight sessions of war and oil risk with no way to react intraday stretches the gap tail. Liquidity also thins from Thursday afternoon.
Sep FOMC · 9/15–16 & CPI · 9/11 — hike odds are a coin-flip after Waller’s dovish shift; next week’s CPI is the cleaner signal. Any spread must clear these dates.
Oil & the 10-year — WTI near $92 keeps inflation fear alive even as yields eased on Waller; a renewed oil pop would push yields and hike odds back up, pressuring stocks.

earnings.intro: The Q2 tail is essentially done — Broadcom (AVGO) and the AI-infra names reported Wednesday/Thursday, and there is no major single-stock print today. The dominant catalyst this session is macro: August nonfarm payrolls at 8:30 ET, then a quiet Labor Day Monday, with CPI (9/11) and the FOMC (9/15–16) the real events next. Keep every spread clear of the jobs print and the FOMC window.
